name: Header
description:
Component: al-header Southleft's primary navigation bar — sticky, translucent, blurred, with pill nav items, circular icon actions and a numbered mobile panel. IT *IS* `al-header` — the brand implementation of that tag, not a wrapper around Altitude's. It owns the `
` landmark, the sticky behaviour and the stacking context itself, and adds what is Southleft's alone: the pill treatment, the icon-button shape, and the mobile panel. It used to compose `` and feed it chrome through `--al-header-background` / `-backdrop-filter` / `-border-block-end`. Taking the tag ended that (one namespace, spec 2026-08-23-one-al-namespace-across-brand-and-base): an `` rendered inside `` recurses forever. Those custom properties are still the public API — header.scss now READS them rather than passing them on — so a consumer overriding one is unaffected. An app gets this implementation, or Altitude's bare landmark, by importing one module or the other. Never both: `customElements.define` is first-come and final. ```html Work Insights Book a call Work ``` It earns its own tag by owning BEHAVIOUR, not arrangement: the mobile panel's open/closed state, the button that drives it, and the `aria-expanded` / `aria-controls` relationship between them. Everything positional is still ``.

props.name: menu-open
props.description:
Whether the mobile panel is open. Reflected so the page can style against
`al-header[menu-open]` and so the state is inspectable in devtools rather
than trapped in the shadow root.

props.name: sticky
props.description: Stick the bar to the top of the scroll container. On by default — the site's header is sticky.

events.name: sl-header-menu-toggle
events.description: When the mobile panel opens or closes. `detail.open` carries the new state.

slots.name: actions
slots.description: The right-hand cluster. Native `<button>`s get the circular icon treatment; anything else (an `<al-button>` CTA) is left alone.

slots.name: mobile
slots.description: The panel's links. Supplied separately from `nav` because a slot can project its nodes only once — see the note in the SCSS.

slots.name: nav
slots.description: The primary links, as flat `<a>` elements. The component gives them the pill treatment and marks `aria-current="page"` as the filled state. Hidden below the `64rem` breakpoint, where the mobile panel takes over.
